UN's Guterres warns AI outpacing oversight, urges global rules to protect children
Olivia Le Poidevin
5-6 分鐘
Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty at U.N.headquarters in New York City
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres speaks to delegates during a meeting on Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty at U.N.headquarters in New York City, U.S., April 27, 2026.

REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz/File Photo Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab
Summary
Companies
Guterres urges globally harmonised AI rules
Calls for AI safety pledge to protect children
First ever UN-led global meeting on AI governance in Geneva
AI development concentrated in US, China;developing countries ​lag
GENEVA, July 6 (Reuters) - U.N.

Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Monday warned that artificial intelligence is developing faster than anyone can ‌keep up, calling for globally harmonised rules to reduce potential risks - especially to children."A technology that can reshape economies, transform the world of work, sway elections and tilt the balance of security is being deployed faster than anyone, including the people building it, can keep up," Guterres told delegates at the first-ever government-level global dialogue on AI in Geneva.

Learn about the latest breakthroughs in AI and tech with the Reuters Artificial Intelligencer newsletter.Sign up here."Innovation needs ​guardrails … If AI is to be powerful, it must be governed," Guterres told delegates.The two-day inaugural U.N.Global Dialogue on AI Governance is ​not intended to forge a treaty, but to discuss how to set rules to mitigate the potential harms of ⁠AI and take advantage of its opportunities.

Delegates will consider a report by a U.N.-backed independent scientific panel of 40 experts, who will present findings from the first ​global, independent scientific assessment of AI.A more comprehensive report is planned next year, alongside a second global meeting in New York.NEED FOR GLOBAL RULES ON AI
Guterres ​stressed that globally harmonised rules on AI must prioritise safety for children after examples of minors being steered towards self-harm and being deceived by machines posing as friends.

"We do not let medicine reach a child until it is proven safe.We test every toy.Yet AI has reached our children – their learning, their friendships, their most private questions – before ​anyone asked what it would do to them," he said.He called for an AI Child Safety Pledge, where companies building systems would have to prove ​they are safe before making them accessible to children.

Systems should also not be allowed to generate sexual images of children, and when a child shows signs of distress, the ‌system should ⁠stop and connect them to a human for help.While AI poses significant opportunities, such as in healthcare, Guterres said the world's institutions were not prepared for machines that make decisions, and that AI's breakneck speed of development meant machines were increasingly making choices with little human or government oversight.

"The internet took 15 years to reach a billion people.AI got there in two," Guterres told delegates.He also warned about the concentration of the most advanced AI systems within ​a handful of companies and countries, ​meaning developing countries have little say ⁠in the progress of AI and risk being left behind.The independent report of scientific experts found that AI development is even more concentrated, with the U.S.

accounting for 75% of the computing power among the world's top 500 AI ​supercomputers, and China 15%.While globally over a billion people now use conversational AI weekly, adoption in developing countries ​lags, the report added.BRIDGING ⁠AI GAP
Guterres said that if used well, AI could compress decades of development into years, potentially becoming "the great equalizer of the twenty-first century".

The head of Libya's Presidential Council, Mohamed al-Menfi, urged that the AI gap be closed in Africa, which accounts for 10% of the world's population but only possesses fewer than 2% of ⁠global data centres."AI ​cannot be a legitimate resource if African countries cannot make use of it," he said, ​calling for greater participation of African states in the design of AI rules.

Georgian President Mikheil Kavelashvili told delegates that world leaders also had a shared responsibility to create robust international laws to ​prevent the power of AI from becoming an "instrument of totalitarian control and new digital tyranny".Reporting by Olivia Le Poidevin, Editing by Miranda Murray and Andrei Khalip

reuters.com
UN's Guterres warns AI outpacing oversight, urges global rules to protect children
Olivia Le Poidevin
5-6 分鐘
Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty at U.N. headquarters in New York City
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres speaks to delegates during a meeting on Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty at U.N. headquarters in New York City, U.S., April 27, 2026. REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz/File Photo Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab
Summary
Companies
Guterres urges globally harmonised AI rules
Calls for AI safety pledge to protect children
First ever UN-led global meeting on AI governance in Geneva
AI development concentrated in US, China; developing countries ​lag
GENEVA, July 6 (Reuters) - U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Monday warned that artificial intelligence is developing faster than anyone can ‌keep up, calling for globally harmonised rules to reduce potential risks - especially to children.
"A technology that can reshape economies, transform the world of work, sway elections and tilt the balance of security is being deployed faster than anyone, including the people building it, can keep up," Guterres told delegates at the first-ever government-level global dialogue on AI in Geneva.
Learn about the latest breakthroughs in AI and tech with the Reuters Artificial Intelligencer newsletter. Sign up here.
"Innovation needs ​guardrails … If AI is to be powerful, it must be governed," Guterres told delegates.
The two-day inaugural U.N. Global Dialogue on AI Governance is ​not intended to forge a treaty, but to discuss how to set rules to mitigate the potential harms of ⁠AI and take advantage of its opportunities.
Delegates will consider a report by a U.N.-backed independent scientific panel of 40 experts, who will present findings from the first ​global, independent scientific assessment of AI.
A more comprehensive report is planned next year, alongside a second global meeting in New York.
NEED FOR GLOBAL RULES ON AI
Guterres ​stressed that globally harmonised rules on AI must prioritise safety for children after examples of minors being steered towards self-harm and being deceived by machines posing as friends.
"We do not let medicine reach a child until it is proven safe. We test every toy. Yet AI has reached our children – their learning, their friendships, their most private questions – before ​anyone asked what it would do to them," he said.
He called for an AI Child Safety Pledge, where companies building systems would have to prove ​they are safe before making them accessible to children.
Systems should also not be allowed to generate sexual images of children, and when a child shows signs of distress, the ‌system should ⁠stop and connect them to a human for help.
While AI poses significant opportunities, such as in healthcare, Guterres said the world's institutions were not prepared for machines that make decisions, and that AI's breakneck speed of development meant machines were increasingly making choices with little human or government oversight.
"The internet took 15 years to reach a billion people. AI got there in two," Guterres told delegates.
He also warned about the concentration of the most advanced AI systems within ​a handful of companies and countries, ​meaning developing countries have little say ⁠in the progress of AI and risk being left behind.
The independent report of scientific experts found that AI development is even more concentrated, with the U.S. accounting for 75% of the computing power among the world's top 500 AI ​supercomputers, and China 15%.
While globally over a billion people now use conversational AI weekly, adoption in developing countries ​lags, the report added.
BRIDGING ⁠AI GAP
Guterres said that if used well, AI could compress decades of development into years, potentially becoming "the great equalizer of the twenty-first century".
The head of Libya's Presidential Council, Mohamed al-Menfi, urged that the AI gap be closed in Africa, which accounts for 10% of the world's population but only possesses fewer than 2% of ⁠global data centres.
"AI ​cannot be a legitimate resource if African countries cannot make use of it," he said, ​calling for greater participation of African states in the design of AI rules.
Georgian President Mikheil Kavelashvili told delegates that world leaders also had a shared responsibility to create robust international laws to ​prevent the power of AI from becoming an "instrument of totalitarian control and new digital tyranny".
Reporting by Olivia Le Poidevin, Editing by Miranda Murray and Andrei Khalip

# reuters.com

reuters.com
聯合國秘書長古特雷斯警告 AI 發展速度超前監管，呼籲制定全球規則保護兒童
Olivia Le Poidevin
5-6 分鐘
在紐約市聯合國總部舉行的《核不擴散條約》會議
聯合國秘書長安東尼奧・古特雷斯於 2026 年 4 月 27 日，在美國紐約市聯合國總部舉行的《核不擴散條約》會議上向代表發言。

路透社／Eduardo Munoz／資料照片　購買授權權利，會在新分頁開啟
摘要
公司
古特雷斯呼籲制定全球協調一致的 AI 規則
呼籲提出 AI 安全承諾以保護兒童
聯合國首次主導的 AI 治理全球會議在日內瓦登場
AI 發展集中在美國與中國；開發中國家落後
日內瓦，7 月 6 日（路透社）——聯合國秘書長安東尼奧・古特雷斯週一警告，人工智慧（AI）的發展速度快到沒有人跟得上，並呼籲制定全球協調一致的規則，以降低潛在風險，尤其是對兒童的風險。

「一項能重塑經濟、改變工作世界、影響選舉並改變安全平衡的技術，正在以比任何人都跟得上的速度被部署，包括打造它的人在內，」古特雷斯在日內瓦首次舉行的政府層級 AI 全球對話中告訴各國代表。

透過路透社 Artificial Intelligencer 電子報掌握 AI 與科技的最新突破。點此訂閱。

「創新需要護欄……如果 AI 要變得強大，就必須受到治理，」古特雷斯告訴各國代表。為期兩天、首次舉行的聯合國 AI 治理全球對話，目的不是要制定條約，而是討論如何訂定規則，以降低 AI 可能造成的危害，並善用其機會。

與會代表將審議一份由聯合國支持、由 40 名專家組成的獨立科學小組所提出的報告；該小組將公布首份全球、獨立的 AI 科學評估結果。更完整的報告預計明年發布，屆時也將在紐約舉行第二場全球會議。

AI 需要全球規則
古特雷斯強調，全球協調一致的 AI 規則必須優先保障兒童安全；此前已有未成年人被引導走向自我傷害，以及被假扮成朋友的機器欺騙的案例。

「藥品未經證明安全前，我們不會讓它接觸兒童。我們會測試每一件玩具。然而，在有人問過 AI 會對孩子造成什麼影響之前，AI 已經接觸到我們的孩子，包括他們的學習、友誼，以及最私密的問題，」他說。他呼籲制定「AI 兒童安全承諾」（AI Child Safety Pledge），要求建置系統的公司在讓兒童使用前，必須先證明系統是安全的。

系統也不應被允許生成兒童的性影像；當兒童出現痛苦跡象時，系統應停止互動，並將他們轉介給真人協助。古特雷斯表示，AI 雖然帶來重大機會，例如在醫療保健領域，但全球制度尚未準備好面對會做決策的機器；而 AI 發展速度極快，也意味著機器越來越常在缺乏人類或政府監督的情況下做出選擇。

「網際網路花了 15 年才觸及 10 億人。AI 只花了兩年，」古特雷斯告訴與會代表。他也警告，最先進的 AI 系統集中在少數公司與國家手中，代表開發中國家對 AI 發展幾乎沒有發言權，也面臨被拋在後面的風險。由獨立科學專家提出的報告發現，AI 發展的集中程度甚至更高，其中美國

占全球前 500 大 AI 超級電腦運算能力的 75%，中國則占 15%。報告並指出，全球目前每週已有超過 10 億人使用對話式 AI，但開發中國家的採用程度仍然落後。

弭平 AI 落差

古特雷斯表示，如果善加運用，AI 可能把數十年的發展壓縮到數年內完成，並有機會成為「二十一世紀偉大的平衡器」。

利比亞總統委員會主席穆罕默德・曼菲（Mohamed al-Menfi）呼籲縮小非洲的 AI 落差。非洲占全球人口 10%，但擁有的全球資料中心不到 2%。「如果非洲國家無法使用 AI，AI 就不可能成為一項正當資源，」他說，並呼籲讓非洲國家更深入參與 AI 規則的制定。

喬治亞總統 Mikheil Kavelashvili 告訴與會代表，世界各國領袖也有共同責任，建立健全的國際法，防止 AI 的力量成為「極權控制與新型數位暴政的工具」。

Olivia Le Poidevin 報導；Miranda Murray 與 Andrei Khalip 編輯
我們的準則：Thomson Reuters Trust Principles，於新分頁開啟
